intro: Jenkinsburg's rural-acreage lots — house plus barns, sheds, and equipment buildings — give the striped skunk (Mephitis mephitis) plenty of places to den, and in central Georgia it stays active right through winter rather than holing up. Add grub-rich lawns to forage and brush for cover and you have steady skunk pressure across this small northern-Butts community. Because the striped skunk is one of Georgia's primary rabies carriers, and because a startled one sprays, removal here belongs with a licensed contractor.
extendedBody:
Start Here: Don't Trap During Kit Season

The most important thing to know before doing anything about a Jenkinsburg skunk is the calendar. From roughly February through May, female striped skunks raise immobile kits under decks, porches, sheds, and outbuildings. Trap out or seal out the mother in that window and the litter is stranded to die in the den — an inhumane outcome and a worse odor and contamination problem than the skunk that prompted the call. During and near kit season the correct approach is eviction: the family is encouraged to leave on its own, and the den is sealed only after it is confirmed empty. Outside that window, humane trapping and removal is the direct route.

Why Jenkinsburg Lots Hold Skunks

This is a very small community built on large rural lots, and that multi-structure layout is the draw. A skunk will den beneath whichever building offers an open, sheltered gap at grade — the house crawlspace, yes, but just as often a barn, shed, or equipment building. The surrounding farmed and pine-hardwood acreage supports the population, the lawns supply grubs (the source of the cone-shaped overnight digs), and woodpiles and brush give daytime cover. Skunks return to a known den site year after year, so an entry left open invites the problem back.

Leave the Trapping to a Pro

  • A do-it-yourself trap usually ends in a spray. A cornered or trap-stressed skunk discharges, and a hit under or against a building drives oily odor into the crawlspace, the structure, and any HVAC intake. Getting a skunk out without triggering that takes experience.
  • Rabies risk is real. The striped skunk is a leading rabies vector in Georgia, and live-trapping means handling and transporting the animal under state regulation — reason enough to keep your distance.
  • The durable fix is trap-or-evict, then exclude. After the animal is gone, the under-structure access is closed with 1/4-inch galvanized hardware cloth trenched down and angled outward so a skunk cannot re-excavate the entry.

Sealing a Whole Jenkinsburg Property

On these lots, doing only the house leaves the skunk a half-dozen other front doors, so prevention is property-wide:

  • Seal every structure — house, barns, sheds, and equipment buildings — along the skirt with buried, outward-angled hardware cloth.
  • Knock back grubs to remove the food that brings a skunk onto the lawn in the first place.
  • Secure trash and pet food and clear fallen fruit and birdseed.
  • Move woodpiles and brush off the structures to take away the ready-made daytime cover. Trapping, eviction, and commercial exclusion all fall under Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division licensing.

faqs.q: How much does skunk removal cost in Jenkinsburg?
faqs.a: The price tracks the season and how many structures need sealing. A straightforward trap-and-remove from under one building outside kit season is the low end; a kit-season eviction, or a Jenkinsburg lot where the house plus several outbuildings all need their skirting closed, runs higher. Spray cleanup is separate. An inspection gives a firm figure.

Apart from the spray, the real concern is rabies — the striped skunk is one of Georgia's primary carriers — so a skunk denning against an occupied home is a public-health issue, not just a smell. Keep people and pets clear of the animal and the den and let a licensed contractor remove it.

faqs.q: There's a skunk under my Jenkinsburg shed — what should I do?
faqs.a: Keep away from it and don't seal the opening yet. In late winter and spring there are probably kits inside, so the den is cleared by eviction and closed only once it's confirmed empty; outside that window it's trapped and removed. Either way the gap is then sealed with buried hardware cloth so it can't be re-dug.

faqs.q: What time of year do skunks have kits near Jenkinsburg?
faqs.a: Roughly February through May. During that window females are raising immobile young under decks, porches, sheds, and outbuildings, which is exactly why trapping or sealing out the mother then is the wrong move — eviction is used instead until the kits can travel.

faqs.q: Does tomato juice work on skunk spray?
faqs.a: No — it only covers the smell. Enzyme-based deodorizers are far more effective on a sprayed pet, and spray that has soaked into a crawlspace or outbuilding generally needs professional oxidizing treatment to clear it from the enclosed space.
